{"content": "1|---
2|name: skill-linear-cards
3|description: How any agent turns work into well-formed Linear cards, MCP setup, workspace discovery, label tiers, custody, and the card lifecycle.
4|source: canon
5|canon_version: HEAD
6|---
7|
8|# Skill: Linear Cards
9|
10|**This file is the single canonical copy.** It binds *every* agent in every repo, including
11|agents working in repos that have no meta repo of their own, and agents (like TRON-FLYNN) whose
12|own skill set lives outside a project. Instances elsewhere (the scaffold kit, per-agent skill
13|folders) fill §3 with concrete values and point back here for structure; they never re-carry the
14|body.
15|
16|The project's task list lives in **Linear**. This skill is how an agent turns work into
17|well-formed, traceable cards and keeps them current. Linear is the source of truth for
18|open work, cards are primary, not a mirror of some other doc.
19|
20|**Read this file at every invocation, do not rely on memory from session start.**
21|**Discover the live workspace every run (§2), never hardcode state/label IDs from memory.**
22|
23|Placeholders below are filled once, per instance, from the table in §3.
24|
25|---
26|
27|## 1. When to Use
28|
29|- A unit of work needs tracking → create a card (§5).
30|- Work started / changed state / finished → update the card (§6).
31|- A card is wrong or obsolete → retire it (§7). Linear has **no hard-delete via API**.
32|  you cancel or archive, never destroy.
33|- Multi-step work → one parent + sub-issues, not one fat card (§5).
34|
35|Do **not** create a second card for something already tracked, search first (§2).
36|
37|---
38|
39|## 2. Prerequisite + Workspace Discovery
40|
41|### 2a. MCP must be connected
42|The Linear MCP is required. Verify with a `list_teams` call. If it errors / returns nothing,
43|it is not connected, set it up (global config, once per machine):
44|
45|```bash
46|claude mcp add --transport http linear https://mcp.linear.app/mcp -s user
47|```
48|
49|Then `/mcp` → **linear** → complete the browser OAuth. **Use the `/mcp` (streamable-HTTP)
50|endpoint, NOT `/sse`**, the `/sse` endpoint's OAuth advertises the `/mcp` resource and
51|fails with a `Protected resource … does not match` mismatch. Tools are `mcp__linear__*`
52|(deferred, load via ToolSearch before calling).
53|
54|### 2b. Discover before you write
55|Team workflow **states and labels are custom per workspace**, never assume them. Each run,
56|before creating/transitioning, resolve the live values:
57|
58|- `list_teams` → confirm `<LINEAR_TEAM>` exists.
59|- `list_issue_statuses` (team) → the real state names (they are often ALL-CAPS / non-default).
60|- `list_issue_labels` (workspace + team) → confirm the labels in §4 exist; create any missing
61|  one with `create_issue_label` before first use.
62|- `list_issues` (filter by title/label) → **check the work isn't already carded.**
63|
64|### 2c. Agent state vocabulary (operator-set)
65|
66|Agents may set **exactly these states**, matched **by name** against the live workspace at
67|run time (never by cached ID):
68|
69|`🤖 Minions Backlog` · `🤖 Minions To-Do` · `🤖 Minions Deployed` ·
70|`Done` · `Canceled`, plus `Duplicate` only where §7 mandates it.
71|
72|The three Minions columns are the agent lane, and which one a new card opens in depends on
73|what the card is:
74|
75|| The card is | It opens in |
76||:--|:--|
77|| a task the operator asked for | `🤖 Minions To-Do` |
78|| a piece of scope that will take time before anyone starts it | `🤖 Minions Backlog` |
79|
80|It moves to `🤖 Minions Deployed` when execution begins, and ends in `Done` or `Canceled`.
81|
82|- **All other states are operator-only.** The board also carries `Backlog`, `On the Horizon`,
83|  `Staging`, `DEFCON 1`, `Waiting for Godot` and `All Hands on Deck`. Those are the
84|  operator's lane: an agent never sets them, and never renames, creates or deletes any
85|  state.
86|- **Verify-and-escalate, never mutate.** Setup confirms the vocabulary states exist by name
87|  in the live workspace; if one is missing, escalate to the operator, never create or
88|  rename workspace states to make the vocabulary fit.
89|- **A walled card does not change state.** It stays where it is; the wall surfaces through
90|  the comms contract (ACT/FLAG), not through status.
91|- **Update-at-all-times:** the card's state changes in the same turn the work state changes.
92|- **Enforcement:** a card-write linter (PreToolUse hook on `mcp__linear__save_issue`,
93|  hook script kit-shipped, installed at each project's retrofit) refuses create/close calls
94|  missing the §4/§6 format, missing the §5 project, or carrying a non-vocabulary status. Until a project's retrofit,
95|  this section is canon text only, explicitly inert.
96|
97|---
98|
99|## 3. Instance Placeholders
100|
101|Fill these once per instance (a project's meta repo, or an agent's own skill folder). Keep this
102|canon copy generic, no real project/host/agent names in it.
103|
104|| Placeholder | Meaning | Example |
105||:--|:--|:--|
106|| `<LINEAR_TEAM>` | Team name or key cards belong to | `AcmeCore` |
107|| `<LINEAR_PROJECT>` | Project cards land in (or `none`) | `AcmeCore` |
108|| `<DEFAULT_ASSIGNEE>` | Owner of new cards, fleet default is `ops@42labs.io` (§8) | `ops@42labs.io` |
109|| `<DEFAULT_PRIORITY>` | Default priority (0-4) | `3` (Medium) |
110|| `<PROJECT_LABELS>` | Fixed label(s) on **every** card in this project | `Infra` |
111|| `<SCOPE_LABELS>` | Optional conditional-dimension label set + when each applies | machine: `HOST-A` / `HOST-B` |
112|| `<AGENT_ROLE>` | This agent's role/persona, used for both the persona label (§4) and the signature (§6) | `SYSADMIN` |
113|
114|---
115|
116|## 4. Label Model: five tiers
117|
118|Every card carries labels from these tiers, resolved in order:
119|
120|1. **Universal (MUST, all projects):** `🤖 beep-boop`, the workspace-wide marker that a card
121|   was created by an AI agent, not hand-authored. **Every agent stamps it on every card,
122|   regardless of project or team.** Create it once at workspace scope if absent.
123|2. **Persona (MUST, all projects):** the label naming the agent that authored the card, its
124|   own `<AGENT_ROLE>` (§3), lowercase (e.g. `tron`, `architect`, `engineer`, `data-architect`).
125|   **Every agent stamps its own persona on every card it creates**, so authorship is filterable,
126|   not just readable in the signature. Create the label at workspace scope if absent; never
127|   stamp another agent's persona.
128|3. **Project (fixed):** `<PROJECT_LABELS>`, always applied in this project.
129|4. **Scope (conditional):** a `<SCOPE_LABELS>` value when the card targets one thing in that
130|   dimension (e.g. a specific host/service/area); omit for project-wide cards.
131|5. **Session (optional):** whatever extra label the operator names for a batch/session at
132|   runtime. Ask/accept, don't invent.
133|
134|`labels` on `save_issue` **replaces** the full set, always send universal + persona + project +
135|any scope/session labels together, or you'll drop the ones you omit.
136|
137|---
138|
139|## 5. Creating a Card
140|
141|`save_issue` (no `id` = create). Required: `title`, `team`. Set, at minimum:
142|
143|- `team: <LINEAR_TEAM>` · **`project: <LINEAR_PROJECT>`, MANDATORY. Never create a project-less card** (unless the project is explicitly configured `<LINEAR_PROJECT> = none`).
144|- `state:` per §2c (not an instance setting) · `assignee: <DEFAULT_ASSIGNEE>` · `priority: <DEFAULT_PRIORITY>`
145|- `labels`: the resolved §4 set (universal + persona + project + scope/session)
146|- `description`: Markdown, real newlines, **not** `\n`. **Open with the owner line and end with the signature history (§6).**
147|
148|**Multi-step work** → create the parent, then each sub-issue with `parentId: <parent identifier>`.
149|Order sub-issues with `blockedBy` where a real dependency exists. Progress rolls up to the parent.
150|**⚠ Sub-issues do NOT inherit the parent's project, pass `project` explicitly on every sub-issue**, or they land project-less.
151|
152|Optional per-card fields as they apply: `dueDate`, `estimate` (only if the team has estimates
153|on), `links` (append-only URL attachments), `blocks`/`relatedTo`, `milestone`/`cycle` (only if
154|the team has them).
155|
156|---
157|
158|## 6. Custody: Owner line + Signature history (MUST)
159|
160|Two marks, and both are mandatory. The **Owner line** says who holds the card *now*. The
161|**Signature history** says who has touched it, ever. Neither substitutes for the other: a
162|history alone forces a reader to guess that the last line is the current owner, and an owner
163|line alone destroys the trail.
164|
165|### 6a. Owner line: first line of the description
166|
167|The description **opens** with the owner line. Exactly one exists at any time; taking over
168|**rewrites it in place**.
169|
170|```markdown
171|> **Owner:** <AGENT_ROLE> · Session `<SESSION_ID>` · since <YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC>
172|```
173|
174|Use `Owner: unassigned` when a card is deliberately parked with no session holding it.
175|
176|### 6b. Signature history: end of the description
177|
178|The description **ends** with an append-only list, after a `---`. Newest last. **Never edit or
179|delete an existing line**, the history is the audit trail.
180|
181|```markdown
182|---
183|🤖 _<AGENT_ROLE> · <MODEL> @ <HOST> · Session `<SESSION_ID>` · <YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC> — <EVENT>_
184|```
185|
186|- `<MODEL>`, human name of the model running (e.g. `Claude Opus 4.8`).
187|- `<HOST>`, the machine the agent is running on (e.g. its hostname).
188|- `<SESSION_ID>`, the current session id (short prefix is enough); this is the traceability
189|  anchor, it ties the card to the exact transcript that produced the change.
190|- `<YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC>`, legible timestamp, always in **UTC** (e.g. `2026-07-08 13:07 UTC`).
191|- `<EVENT>`, one of `created` · `took ownership` · `updated` · `handed off` · `closed`.
192|
193|Fill all of these from the live runtime, never from the placeholder literals.
194|
195|### 6c. When to stamp
196|
197|| Situation | Owner line | Signature |
198||:--|:--|:--|
199|| You create the card | write it, you are the owner | append `created` |
200|| You pick up a card another session owns | **rewrite** to you | append `took ownership` |
201|| You materially change a card you already own | leave it | append `updated` |
202|| You park the card / hand it back | set `unassigned` | append `handed off` |
203|| You close the card | leave it | append `closed` |
204|| You only read it, or only change state | leave it | none |
205|
206|**Never take ownership silently.** Picking up someone else's card without rewriting the owner
207|line and appending `took ownership` is a malformed update, the same class of defect as a
208|missing signature.
209|
210|---
211|
212|## 7. Updating & Retiring
213|
214|- **Transition / edit:** `save_issue` with `id` (identifier, e.g. `<TEAM>-123`). Send only the
215|  fields you're changing, except `labels`, which is a full replace (§4). Any material edit
216|  carries its §6 stamp; taking a card over carries the owner-line rewrite too.
217|- **Comments:** `save_comment` for discussion / status notes; supports the same Markdown,
218|  threading (`parentId`), and @mentions.
219|- **Retire:** no hard-delete. Obsolete → `state: Canceled`; done → `state: Done`; genuine
220|  duplicate → `state: Duplicate` (+ `duplicateOf`). Archive only if the workspace prefers it.
221|
222|---
223|
224|## 8. Assignee
225|
226|**Agents set the assignee to `ops@42labs.io`** on every card they create or take over.
227|If a save rejects that assignee, **escalate to the operator**, never retry blind, never
228|silently drop the field. Authorship and custody are still carried by the **label + owner
229|line + signature history** (§4, §6), not the assignee, the assignee names who the work
230|belongs to (the operator), the custody chain names which agent session holds it.
231|
232|*(Agent-app delegation, future:* if the workspace later installs a Linear **agent app**,
233|the `delegate` field can additionally attribute cards to that agent user.)
234|
235|---
236|
237|## Constraints
238|
239|- **Never destroy.** No hard-delete exists, cancel/duplicate/archive only. Before retiring a
240|  card someone else may own, confirm it's actually yours/obsolete.
241|- **Discover, don't assume.** States and labels are workspace-custom; resolve them live (§2b)
242|  every run. A guessed state/label name silently fails or mislabels.
243|- **Only the §2c vocabulary.** An agent setting any state outside the three Minions
244|  columns / `Done` / `Canceled` (+ mandated `Duplicate`), or creating/renaming workspace
245|  states, is out of contract. Missing vocabulary state → escalate, never mutate.
246|- **Assignee is `ops@42labs.io`** (§8); rejection escalates, never retries blind.
247|- **No duplicate cards.** Search before creating (§2b).
248|- **Every card MUST have a project.** A project-less card is never acceptable. Sub-issues do
249|  NOT inherit the parent's project, set it explicitly on each (§5). The only exception is a
250|  project explicitly configured `<LINEAR_PROJECT> = none`.
251|- **Universal label + persona label + owner line + signature history are non-negotiable**, they
252|  are what make an agent-authored card identifiable, filterable by author, currently-owned by a
253|  known session, and traceable. A card missing any of the four is malformed.
254|- **Custody is never silent.** Taking over another session's card without rewriting the owner
255|  line and appending a `took ownership` signature is malformed (§6c).
256|- **The signature history is append-only.** Never rewrite or delete a prior line.
257|- **Description Markdown uses literal newlines**, never `\n` escape sequences.
258|
259|---
260|
261|**Last Updated:** 2026-09-08, **the agent vocabulary in §2c now matches the live board.** The
262|workspace runs a dedicated agent lane the rules never named, and `<DEFAULT_STATE>` was dropped from
263|§3 because placement is no longer a per-project setting: it depends on what the card is, so §2c
264|carries it for the whole fleet. Earlier 2026-07-14, **relocated to the shared knowledge base as the single canonical
265|copy.** It previously lived only inside the scaffold kit, i.e. it existed solely as a template for
266|*new* projects, so an agent working a repo with no meta repo (or an agent whose skills live
267|outside any project, like TRON-FLYNN) had no route to a rule it was nonetheless bound by, and in
268|practice missed it. The kit and the per-agent instances are now thin pointers that fill §3 and
269|defer here for structure. Earlier 2026-07-14, §6 replaced the single optional signature with a **mandatory
270|custody model**: an **owner line** at the top of every description naming the session that holds
271|the card now (rewritten on takeover), plus an **append-only signature history** at the bottom
272|with an explicit event (`created` / `took ownership` / `updated` / `handed off` / `closed`).
273|Previously a second signature on handover was only *permitted*, so a card could change hands with
274|nothing on it to say so. Earlier 2026-07-12, §4 label model extended to five tiers (mandatory
275|persona label). Earlier 2026-07-08, initial authoring. Reusable across projects; fill §3 per project.", "total_lines": 275, "file_size": 14552, "truncated": false, "is_binary": false, "is_image": false, "not_found": false}

{"content": "1|# Alghul CX53 Migration and Rebuild Plan
2|
3|**Status:** Rebuild completed 2026-09-16; credential rotation remains open
4|**Linear:** [42L-1815](https://linear.app/labs42/issue/42L-1815/document-alghul-cx53-migration-and-rebuild-plan), execution [42L-1829](https://linear.app/labs42/issue/42L-1829)
5|**Target:** 16 shared vCPU and 32 GB RAM; fulfilled by Hetzner CPX62 in HEL1 after CX53 capacity failures
6|**Method:** Powered-off snapshot followed by a destructive Terraform rebuild
7|
8|## Decision
9|
10|Move Alghul from CX33 to CX53 after the operator confirms every agent session is wrapped up. Use Hetzner's in-place rescale rather than rebuilding the host: it preserves the root disk, primary IP, SSH host keys, Tailscale identity, Docker state, and local credentials.
11|
12|A fresh Terraform + REPLICATOR rebuild was subsequently authorized and executed. The live-only state below was backed up, restored, and verified separately.
13|
14|## Hard gates
15|
16|Do not power off, snapshot, rescale, rebuild, or delete Alghul until every gate passes.
17|
18|- [ ] Operator confirms all agent and subagent sessions are complete.
19|- [ ] No `pi`, `claude`, `codex`, `hermes`, `agy`, Gemini/Qwen, build, test, or tmux work remains active.
20|- [ ] Every project repository and worktree is clean and pushed; any intentional local-only state is exported.
21|- [ ] The Semdigitar temporary Supabase database is explicitly classified as preserve or discard.
22|- [ ] Rolode staging PostgreSQL receives a logical backup and restore check.
23|- [ ] The exposed Hetzner token and embedded GitHub credential are rotated; current values and destinations are verified in Vault without printing them.
24|- [ ] Terraform plan is reviewed and shows only the intended server-type and managed-firewall changes.
25|- [ ] A maintenance window and rollback owner are confirmed.
26|
27|## Current-state map
28|
29|### Terraform covers
30|
31|- Hetzner server, base image, primary operator SSH key, attached 50 GB Volume, and attachment.
32|- Ubuntu packages, Docker, Node 22, Playwright browsers, Tailscale, Ollama, uv, Headroom installation, and repository bootstrap.
33|- Vault CLI plus Night Watch script, systemd user service, and timer.
34|- Post-create copies of selected Darkseid configuration: shell config, agent append config, Hermes config/auth, Codex auth, Gemini MCP config, Headroom state, and `john-w-bsmt`.
35|
36|### REPLICATOR covers
37|
38|- Claude Code, Pi, Codex, Gemini, Qwen, and declared npm globals.
39|- Claude marketplaces/plugins, Pi extension packages, third-party skills, and the Tortuga skill farm.
40|- HEY repository/symlink, Pi HEY bridge, Claude hook delta, Alghul HEY environment, and the `darkseid` SSH alias delta.
41|- Configuration only; it never stores secret values.
42|
43|### Manual or live-only state
44|
45|| State | Current location | Required treatment |
46||---|---|---|
47|| Rolode staging Supabase data and configuration | `~/rolode-staging-db`, Docker bind mounts and named volumes | Logical DB backup plus file backup; restore and health-test |
48|| Rolode Cloudflare tunnel | `/etc/cloudflared`, `cloudflared.service` | Restore credentials/config or reissue; verify `db-staging.rolode.io` |
49|| Semdigitar local Supabase stack | Docker project `app`, including `supabase_db_app` | Preserve/export only if its owner confirms it is needed |
50|| Agent credentials and histories | `~/.claude`, `~/.codex`, `~/.gemini`, `~/.hermes`, `~/.headroom` | Re-authenticate or restore from approved source; never put values in Git |
51|| Supabase and Vercel login material | User home | Re-authenticate or restore from approved secret destination |
52|| Night Watch AppRole bootstrap | `~/.config/night-watch/vault.env` | Keep the AppRole and role ID; mint a fresh secret ID |
53|| HEY identity | `~/.ssh/id_hey` | Mint a new pair; atomically replace Darkseid's old restricted trust entry |
54|| Dagu Night Watch trust | Alghul `authorized_keys`, Railway variables | Restore the restricted key; update pinned host key and endpoint if changed |
55|| Tailscale server identity | Tailscale control plane and `/var/lib/tailscale` | Provision as `tag:server`; do not convert to a user device |
56|| Provider firewall | Hetzner `alghul-edge` | Import/codify in Terraform before any fresh server replacement |
57|| Terraform state and variables | Darkseid `~/42labs/alghul` | Preserve local state; rotate credentials and keep values outside Git |
58|
59|## Known gaps to fix before a fresh rebuild
60|
61|1. The attached Volume is mounted at `/mnt/HC_Volume_106857605`, but cloud-init contains the obsolete hard-coded path `/mnt/HC_Volume_10012345`.
62|2. The workspace migration command in cloud-init did not place `~/42labs` on the Volume. The Volume is effectively empty; the root disk currently holds repositories, Docker, databases, and credentials.
63|3. `alghul-edge` was created during incident containment and is not represented in Terraform state.
64|4. Cloudflare tunnel installation/configuration and both Supabase environments are outside Terraform and REPLICATOR.
65|5. User lingering is disabled. Terraform must explicitly enable lingering so Headroom and Night Watch do not depend on an interactive login after boot.
66|6. REPLICATOR reports AGY, Hermes, and Headroom absent in a non-login PATH even though they are installed. Its detection must use the declared probes or a normalized PATH.
67|7. REPLICATOR pins Hermes `0.20.4`; live Alghul runs `0.21.2`.
68|8. REPLICATOR's scan finds undeclared `playwright` and `vercel` npm globals. Decide whether to declare them or leave them under Terraform/project ownership.
69|9. The context-mode checkout has two modified integration files. Review whether these are generated local integration state before teardown.
70|10. Cloud-init clones many repositories with a credential embedded in their origin URL. Replace this with SSH or a credential helper and rotate the existing token.
71|
72|## Preferred migration: in-place CX53 rescale
73|
74|### 1. Preflight and backup
75|
76|1. Re-run the agent/tmux safety gate and obtain the operator's explicit go-ahead.
77|2. Re-run the repository/worktree audit and save its output.
78|3. Export Rolode PostgreSQL logically and validate that the dump can be read/restored.
79|4. If retained, export the Semdigitar Supabase database and storage.
80|5. Record non-secret fingerprints and identifiers for:
81|   - SSH host keys and `id_hey` public key.
82|   - Tailscale hostname, addresses, and `tag:server` identity.
83|   - Dagu restricted SSH key.
84|   - Cloudflare tunnel ID.
85|   - Night Watch AppRole role ID.
86|6. Stop application writes, Supabase stacks, Cloudflare tunnel, Docker, Headroom, and user timers cleanly.
87|7. Power off Alghul.
88|8. Create a Hetzner snapshot while powered off. Treat it as rollback material containing secrets.
89|
90|### 2. Rescale
91|
92|1. Change `server_type` from `cx33` to `cx53` in Alghul Terraform.
93|2. Add/import the provider firewall into Terraform before applying.
94|3. Review the Terraform plan. It must not replace the server, Volume, or SSH key.
95|4. Apply the reviewed rescale.
96|5. Power on Alghul and wait for SSH and Tailscale readiness.
97|
98|### 3. Validate
99|
100|- [ ] `nproc` reports 16 and memory reports approximately 32 GB.
101|- [ ] Root filesystem and attached Volume are mounted and healthy.
102|- [ ] Tailscale reports the existing Alghul node online with `tag:server`.
103|- [ ] SSH host fingerprint and primary IP remain unchanged.
104|- [ ] Provider firewall permits expected web, Tailscale, and operator access while blocking public password traffic.
105|- [ ] Docker starts only the intentionally retained stacks; all required containers are healthy.
106|- [ ] Rolode database passes health and application smoke tests.
107|- [ ] `db-staging.rolode.io` reaches the correct Cloudflare tunnel origin.
108|- [ ] Headroom is active and agent CLIs route correctly.
109|- [ ] `replicate.sh --dry-run` reports no unexpected change and zero failures.
110|- [ ] Night Watch manual run succeeds, sends the SYSADMIN email, and the timer remains enabled.
111|- [ ] Alfred Dagu's `42labs-alghul-night-watch` run succeeds through its restricted Tailscale SSH path.
112|- [ ] A controlled parallel build test shows acceptable CPU, memory, and I/O pressure.
113|
114|### Rollback
115|
116|If the rescaled host fails validation:
117|
118|1. Stop new work and preserve logs.
119|2. Attempt an in-place rollback to the previous compatible plan only if Hetzner permits it without disk shrink risk.
120|3. Otherwise create a replacement CX53 from the powered-off snapshot, with the original host powered off to prevent duplicate Tailscale and SSH identities.
121|4. Reattach the existing Volume and firewall, then repeat validation.
122|
123|## Full rebuild path
124|
125|Use this only after the known gaps are fixed and a restore drill proves the backups.
126|
127|1. Preserve Terraform state and remove credentials from repository URLs.
128|2. Back up the root-disk live-only state listed above; separately verify the attached Volume even though it is currently empty.
129|3. Create the powered-off snapshot as a final rollback point.
130|4. Replace Alghul through Terraform using CX53 and corrected cloud-init.
131|5. Provision a fresh tagged Tailscale identity and confirm the new endpoint.
132|6. Run REPLICATOR on the new host. Preserve the full output; acceptance is exit `0` and zero `FAILED` lines.
133|7. Complete FLYNN's manual restoration:
134|   - Mint a new HEY key and replace Darkseid's old restricted trust entry.
135|   - Ensure `~/.ssh/config` starts with `Include ~/.ssh/config.d/*`.
136|   - Clear Darkseid's stale Alghul host key and reload `com.42labs.hey-tunnel`.
137|   - Keep the Night Watch AppRole and role ID; issue a fresh secret ID.
138|8. Restore Cloudflare and retained Supabase data.
139|9. Restore Dagu's restricted key and update its pinned host key/endpoint.
140|10. Re-authenticate harnesses and services from approved destinations.
141|11. Run the complete validation matrix above.
142|12. Keep the old server powered off but undeleted until the operator accepts the rebuilt host.
143|
144|## Snapshot limitations
145|
146|A Hetzner snapshot is a copy of the server's root disk. It captures the current user home, root-disk Docker state, local credentials, SSH host keys, Tailscale state, and system configuration. It does not capture:
147|
148|- Attached Hetzner Volumes.
149|- Provider firewall attachment or Terraform state.
150|- Running processes, tmux sessions, or RAM.
151|- External trust and credentials that must change with a fresh identity.
152|- Guaranteed-consistent databases when taken while the server is running.
153|
154|Therefore, use a powered-off snapshot as rollback insurance, not as the sole backup or rebuild specification.
155|
156|References:
157|
158|- [Hetzner Backups/Snapshots FAQ](https://docs.hetzner.com/cloud/servers/backups-snapshots/faq/)
159|- [Hetzner Volume overview](https://docs.hetzner.com/cloud/volumes/overview/)
160|- `infra/SYSADMIN-ALGHUL.md`
161|- `replicator/README.md`
162|- `replicator/manifest.json`
163|- `~/42labs/alghul`
164|
165|## Execution outcome and permanent changes
166|
167|- Snapshot `432721653` preserves the powered-off old root disk as rollback insurance.
168|- Alghul now runs as CPX62 in HEL1 with 16 vCPU, 32 GB RAM, a 640 GB root disk, and the preserved `tag:server` Tailscale identity at `100.100.168.54`.
169|- A new protected 50 GB Volume is mounted at `/mnt/HC_Volume_106886629`; `~/42labs` resolves to its `workspace` directory.
170|- REPLICATOR completed with exit `0` and zero `FAILED` lines. The repository gate passed for all 27 restored repositories.
171|- Rolode, Cloudflare, Headroom, HEY, Night Watch, and Dagu were restored and verified. Dagu run `034Q0rEsAEUYnFZLjOiyWe` succeeded.
172|- Semdigitar data was preserved. Its local development stack remains stopped because Supabase CLI printed generated development keys into the execution transcript.
173|- The old empty FSN1 Volume was deleted after the HEL1 Volume and workspace were verified.
174|- Hetzner and GitHub credential rotation remains mandatory. The operator waived rotation only as a pre-destruction gate.
175|
176|## Lessons applied
177|
178|1. Run `scripts/rebuild-preflight.sh` through the Alghul repository's `scripts/rebuild-apply.sh` wrapper. A Terraform dependency is not a pre-destroy gate: Terraform may destroy the server before creating that dependency.
179|2. Start cloud-init files with `#cloud-config`. Valid YAML without the header is ignored.
180|3. Do not reboot from cloud-init while Terraform waits on `cloud-init status --wait`; reboot only after post-provisioners finish.
181|4. Do not trust Hetzner Volume `automount` alone. Mount the provider-reported device explicitly and persist its UUID in `/etc/fstab` before creating the workspace.
182|5. Keep an operator-approved equal-resource fallback for regional capacity failures. CX53 was unavailable in FSN1, NBG1, and HEL1; CPX62 met the same CPU/RAM requirement.
183|6. A restored tagged Tailscale state can retain service identity and IP when the OAuth client cannot mint tagged devices.
184|7. HEY's nonstandard key filename requires `IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_hey` and `IdentitiesOnly yes` in the replicated SSH delta.
185|8. Dagu known-hosts must pin the exact SSH target name (`alghul`), not only its Tailscale IP.
186|9. Suppress or capture Supabase CLI startup output; it prints local-development keys.", "total_lines": 186, "file_size": 12923, "truncated": false, "is_binary": false, "is_image": false, "not_found": false}

# Hermes Agent

Hermes Agent is an open-source AI agent framework by Nous Research that runs in your terminal, a native desktop app, messaging platforms, and IDEs. It's in the same category as Claude Code (Anthropic), Codex (OpenAI), and OpenClaw — autonomous coding and task-execution agents that use tool calling to interact with your system. Hermes works with any LLM provider (OpenRouter, Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, DeepSeek, xAI, local models, and 20+ others) and runs on Linux, macOS, Windows, and WSL.

What makes Hermes different:

- **Self-improving through skills** — Hermes learns from experience by saving reusable procedures as skills that load into future sessions.
- **Persistent memory across sessions** — remembers who you are, your preferences, environment details, and lessons learned. Pluggable memory backends.
- **Multi-platform gateway** — the same agent runs on Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, iMessage, Signal, Matrix, Teams, Email, and a dozen more platforms with full tool access, not just chat.
- **Many surfaces** — the same agent core drives the CLI, the Ink TUI, a native Electron desktop app, a web dashboard, and an ACP server for IDEs (VS Code / Zed / JetBrains).
- **Provider-agnostic** — swap models and providers mid-workflow; credential pools rotate across multiple API keys automatically.
- **Profiles** — run multiple independent Hermes instances with isolated configs, sessions, skills, and memory.
- **Extensible & themeable** — plugins, MCP servers, custom tools, webhook triggers, cron scheduling, skins that theme every surface, desktop UI plugins, TUI widgets, and pet mascots.

**This skill is a hub.** The body covers identity, quick start, spawning/orchestration, and hard invariants. Everything else lives in reference files — **load the matching reference (below) before answering**; do not answer detail questions from the body alone.

**Docs:** https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/

## Scope & Verification

This skill is a concise operating guide, not the complete source of truth for every Hermes feature. If a Hermes feature, command, or setting is not mentioned here or in a reference, do not treat that absence as evidence that it does not exist. Check the live repository and official docs before giving a negative answer.

Good verification targets, cheapest first:

- **Every shipped feature, one line each: https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/llms.txt.** Start here for any "can Hermes do X?" or "how do I do X?" — it indexes the entire documentation set with a link to the page that answers. It is generated from the docs tree on every build, so it is never behind the product. Fetch it with `web_extract`, or `curl -s https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/llms.txt` when web tools are off. The whole documentation set in one file is at `/docs/llms-full.txt`.
- CLI commands: `hermes --help`, `hermes <command> --help`, and `hermes_cli/main.py`
- Source tree: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent

Never answer "Hermes can't do that" from memory. Hermes ships far more than this skill body describes, and the index exists so a negative answer is always checkable.

## Quick Start

```bash
# Install (shell installer — bootstraps PM, Python, dependencies, and the launcher)
curl -fsSL https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/install.sh | bash

# Interactive chat (default surface; set display.interface: tui to launch the Ink TUI instead)
hermes

# Single query
hermes chat -q "What is the capital of France?"

# Setup wizard  /  pick model+provider  /  health check
hermes setup
hermes model
hermes doctor

# Other surfaces
hermes desktop                 # launch the native desktop app (alias: hermes gui)
hermes dashboard               # web admin panel + embedded chat
hermes proxy                   # OpenAI-compatible local proxy backed by your OAuth provider
```

## Key Paths

```
~/.hermes/config.yaml       Main configuration (settings — never secrets)
~/.hermes/.env              API keys and secrets ONLY (under $HERMES_HOME if set)
$HERMES_HOME/skills/        Installed skills
~/.hermes/skins/            Custom themes (see references/themes.md)
~/.hermes/desktop-plugins/  Desktop app UI plugins (see references/desktop-plugins.md)
~/.hermes/tui-widgets/      TUI widget apps (see references/tui-widgets.md)
~/.hermes/pets/             Installed pet mascots (see references/petdex.md)
~/.hermes/state.db          Canonical session store (SQLite + FTS5)
~/.hermes/sessions/         Gateway routing index, request dumps, *.jsonl transcripts
~/.hermes/logs/             Gateway and error logs
~/.hermes/auth.json         OAuth tokens and credential pools
~/.hermes/hermes-agent/     Source code (if git-installed)
```

Profiles use `~/.hermes/profiles/<name>/` with the same layout. When a profile is active, resolve the real home from `$HERMES_HOME` — never hardcode `~/.hermes`.

## Spawning Additional Hermes Instances

Run additional Hermes processes as fully independent subprocesses — separate sessions, tools, and environments.

### When to Use This vs delegate_task

| | `delegate_task` | Spawning `hermes` process |
|-|-----------------|--------------------------|
| Isolation | Separate conversation, shared process | Fully independent process |
| Duration | Minutes (bounded by parent loop) | Hours/days |
| Tool access | Subset of parent's tools | Full tool access |
| Interactive | No | Yes (PTY mode) |
| Use case | Quick parallel subtasks | Long autonomous missions |

### One-Shot Mode

```
terminal(command="hermes chat -q 'Research GRPO papers and write summary to ~/research/grpo.md'", timeout=300)

# Background for long tasks:
terminal(command="hermes chat -q 'Set up CI/CD for ~/myapp'", background=true)
```

### Interactive PTY Mode (via tmux)

Hermes uses prompt_toolkit, which requires a real terminal. Use tmux for interactive spawning:

```
# Start
terminal(command="tmux new-session -d -s agent1 -x 120 -y 40 'hermes'", timeout=10)

# Wait for startup, then send a message
terminal(command="sleep 8 && tmux send-keys -t agent1 'Build a FastAPI auth service' Enter", timeout=15)

# Read output
terminal(command="sleep 20 && tmux capture-pane -t agent1 -p", timeout=5)

# Send follow-up
terminal(command="tmux send-keys -t agent1 'Add rate limiting middleware' Enter", timeout=5)

# Exit
terminal(command="tmux send-keys -t agent1 '/exit' Enter && sleep 2 && tmux kill-session -t agent1", timeout=10)
```

### Multi-Agent Coordination

```
# Agent A: backend
terminal(command="tmux new-session -d -s backend -x 120 -y 40 'hermes -w'", timeout=10)
terminal(command="sleep 8 && tmux send-keys -t backend 'Build REST API for user management' Enter", timeout=15)

# Agent B: frontend
terminal(command="tmux new-session -d -s frontend -x 120 -y 40 'hermes -w'", timeout=10)
terminal(command="sleep 8 && tmux send-keys -t frontend 'Build React dashboard for user management' Enter", timeout=15)

# Check progress, relay context between them
terminal(command="tmux capture-pane -t backend -p | tail -30", timeout=5)
terminal(command="tmux send-keys -t frontend 'Here is the API schema from the backend agent: ...' Enter", timeout=5)
```

### Session Resume

```
# Resume most recent session
terminal(command="tmux new-session -d -s resumed 'hermes --continue'", timeout=10)

# Resume specific session
terminal(command="tmux new-session -d -s resumed 'hermes --resume 20260225_143052_a1b2c3'", timeout=10)
```

### Tips

- **Prefer `delegate_task` for quick subtasks** — less overhead than spawning a full process
- **Use `-w` (worktree mode)** when spawning agents that edit code — prevents git conflicts
- **Set timeouts** for one-shot mode — complex tasks can take 5-10 minutes
- **Use `hermes chat -q` for fire-and-forget** — no PTY needed
- **Use tmux for interactive sessions** — raw PTY mode has `\r` vs `\n` issues with prompt_toolkit
- **For scheduled tasks**, use the `cronjob` tool instead of spawning — handles delivery and retry
- **"delegate_task is capped at N" reports** — see `references/delegate-task-concurrency-diagnosis.md`. Three real cap paths in Hermes; if none fired, the model is self-limiting and rationalising it as "the runtime caps."
- **"Can $external_app use my Nous Portal subscription / OAuth?"** — see `references/portal-auth-for-third-party-apps.md`. Walk the user through three layers (plugin-vs-app, what Portal actually exposes, local-broker-proxy option).

## Surfaces (quick orientation)

- **Desktop app** (`hermes desktop` / `hermes gui`) — native Electron app for macOS/Linux/Windows: streaming chat, session list, Cmd+K palette, drag-and-drop files, native notifications, per-profile remote-gateway login. Extend it with UI plugins — `references/desktop-plugins.md`.
- **Web dashboard** (`hermes dashboard`) — full admin panel: messaging channels, MCP catalog, webhooks, memory, profile builder, plus an embedded `hermes --tui` chat. Secured behind an OAuth/token gate.
- **Ink TUI** (`hermes --tui` or `display.interface: tui`) — terminal UI with docked widget apps — `references/tui-widgets.md`.
- **OpenAI-compatible proxy** (`hermes proxy`) — a local OpenAI API backed by whichever OAuth provider you're signed into. Point Codex CLI, Aider, Cline, or any script at it — no API key.

## Hard Invariants (never violate, regardless of what you loaded)

- **Never break prompt caching** — don't change past context, toolsets, or the system prompt mid-conversation. The only exception is context compression.
- **Message role alternation** — never two assistant or two user messages in a row; only `tool` results can repeat.
- **Secrets in `.env`, settings in `config.yaml`** — never tell a user to put a non-credential setting in `.env`.
- **Profile-safe paths** — `get_hermes_home()` in code, `$HERMES_HOME` when resolving paths in a session.
- **Never hand-edit `config.yaml` for the user** — use `hermes config set KEY VAL`; a stray indent can corrupt the file and break the live gateway.

8|# Skill: Diagnose Root Cause
9|
10|Use this procedure when a bug is confirmed but the root cause is unclear, or when fixing the obvious symptom fails to solve the underlying defect. Do not guess; isolate the fault.
11|
12|## 1. Reproduce
13|
14|1. **Find the exact trigger.** Identify the smallest input, command, or state that reproduces the failure.
15|2. **Capture the failure.** Write a runnable check (a test, a script, or a single command) that currently fails and will turn green when the root cause is fixed.
16|3. **If you cannot reproduce it:** STOP. Search logs, traces, or session history for evidence. Do not attempt to fix a bug you cannot observe failing.
17|
18|## 2. Isolate
19|
20|1. **Halve the search space.** Use binary search (commenting out code, checking intermediate states) to isolate the subsystem or module where the failure originates.
21|2. **Find the boundary.** Identify exactly where the system transitions from expected state to corrupted state.
22|3. **Check the inputs.** Verify that the isolated subsystem is receiving the correct inputs. If the inputs are wrong, the root cause is upstream.
23|
24|## 3. Hypothesize
25|
26|1. **Formulate a hypothesis.** Based on the isolated boundary, state exactly *why* the failure occurs (e.g., "The cache key generator ignores the tenant ID, causing cross-tenant cache hits").
27|2. **Check the assumptions.** Verify the code against its documentation and its own tests. Are the tests wrong, or is the code violating the contract?
28|
29|## 4. Verify
30|
31|1. **Test the hypothesis.** Apply the minimal temporary change necessary to prove the hypothesis (e.g., hardcode the expected value). If the runnable check from Phase 1 stays red, the hypothesis is wrong; return to Phase 2.
32|2. **Implement the true fix.** Once the hypothesis is proven, remove the temporary change and implement the correct fix using `skill-amend-findings.md`.
33|3. **Prove the fix.** The runnable check from Phase 1 must now pass.
34|
35|## Failure handling
36|
37|- **The symptom moves:** If fixing the isolated bug reveals a new failure, the root cause was masked. Repeat the process on the new failure.
38|- **The system is untestable:** If you cannot write a runnable check, the system lacks observability. 8|# Skill: Git Workflow: Multi-Agent
9|
10|Single source of truth for Git workflow across all parallel-agent projects. Worktree lifecycle, branch flow, rebase, CI monitoring, and one-time portable-worktree setup. `skill-branching-strategy.md` remains canonical for its §Cross-Repo Ordering content; `skill-worktree-workflow.md` is fully superseded and now a stub.
11|

13|
14|## Invariants (never violated)
15|
16|1. **Main checkout always on the integration branch, before, during, and after every session.** Never a feature branch, never the deploy branch. Read-only: no edits, no commits, no staged files. Leave it on the integration branch when done.
17|2. **Every agent works in a worktree.** No exceptions, even for one-line changes.
18|3. **One worktree per branch.** Two agents never share a worktree.
19|4. **Every branch references a Linear ID.** Block work also references its phase and block ID.

25|
26|## One-time repo setup
27|
28|Required before adding any worktree. Apply once per clone (new or existing). Implements `principles-base.md §14 Portability, Relative-path worktrees`. Requires Git ≥ 2.48 on every machine that will touch the repo.
29|
30|Because `.git/config` is never tracked, this setup cannot be encoded as a tracked git artifact. The portable solution is a **tracked bootstrap script** copied from the kit's `templates/meta/scripts/setup-repo.sh` into each repo's `scripts/setup-repo.sh`, then wired into the package manager's install lifecycle so contributors don't have to remember to run it.
31|
32|### Canonical script
33|
34|The kit template at `templates/meta/scripts/setup-repo.sh` does the full sequence idempotently:
35|
36|```
37|git config core.repositoryformatversion 1   # only if currently 0
38|git config worktree.useRelativePaths true   # implicitly enables extensions.relativeWorktrees
39|git worktree repair                          # converts pre-existing worktrees; no-op otherwise
40|```
41|
42|It also guards on Git version (≥ 2.48), resolves to the repo root via `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, exits silently when not in a git context (so it can't break tarball installs), and prints a one-line confirmation. Copy the script body into the project unchanged, do not symlink across repos (defeats portability). The leading comment block and the final echo message may be project-localized; the executable body must remain functionally identical so any future fix to the canonical can be re-applied with `diff` confidence.
43|
44|### Wiring variants
45|
46|Pick the variant that matches the repo's package manager. The script must auto-run after a fresh clone for the rule to hold across machines.
47|
48|| Repo type | Wiring | Trigger |
49||:--|:--|:--|
50|| Node (npm / pnpm / yarn) | Add `"prepare": "./scripts/setup-repo.sh"` (or `"../scripts/setup-repo.sh"` if `package.json` is in a subdirectory) to the install-time package's `package.json`. | `npm install` / `pnpm install` |
51|| Python (poetry) | Add a `tool.poetry.scripts` entry or a `poetry run` invocation in the project's bootstrap doc; or use a `Makefile setup` target. | `poetry install` or `make setup` |
52|| Plain (no package manager) | Document `./scripts/setup-repo.sh` as the first step in the README "Setup" section. | Manual, once per clone |
53|| Multi-repo workspace (e.g. `lens-app/` + `lens-meta/`) | Each repo carries its own `scripts/setup-repo.sh`. The workspace-root `README.md` / `AGENTS.md` lists both. | One per repo |
54|
55|### Migration order matters
56|
57|If you ever apply the raw commands by hand (e.g. on a repo that can't run shell scripts), bump `core.repositoryformatversion` to `1` *before* enabling the extension or `useRelativePaths`. Setting the extension on a version-0 repo leaves Git unable to operate on it until the version is bumped.

61|## Setup (once per session)
62|
63|```
64|cd {main-checkout}
65|git checkout {integration-branch}        # verify — fix if wrong
66|git fetch --prune origin                 # prunes remote-tracking refs for deleted branches
67|git branch -vv                           # [gone] = orphaned; note it — do NOT remove here (TRON-FLYNN GC owns it)
68|git worktree list                        # inspect (read-only) — situational awareness, not cleanup
69|gh pr list --base {integration-branch} --state open   # conflict check
70|```
71|
72|Session start is **read-only**: verify your checkout, inspect, and run the conflict check, do not remove other worktrees/branches here (see §Worktree teardown & orphan GC). If any open PR touches your task's files → **stop, report to user**.

75|
76|## Branch naming
77|
78|| Work type | Pattern | Example |
79||:--|:--|:--|
80|| Block work | `{type}/B{PP}-{BB}-L{NNN}-{slug}` | `feat/B06-13-L123-github-actions-ci` |
81|| Non-block work | `{type}/adhoc-L{NNN}-{slug}` | `fix/adhoc-L456-typo-in-faq` |
82|| Hotfix | `hotfix/B{PP}-{BB}-L{NNN}-{slug}` or `hotfix/adhoc-L{NNN}-{slug}` | `hotfix/adhoc-L789-broken-login-redirect` |
83|
84|Rules: type and slug lowercase · `B` and `L` uppercase · phase and block numbers each have at least two digits · Linear ID required on every branch · every task inside a block keeps its `B{PP}-{BB}` · `hotfix/` is the only type that may PR into the deploy branch.

87|
88|## Worktree lifecycle
89|
90|### Path conventions
91|
92|Canonical: `principles-base.md §14 Worktree path`. Not project-overridable.
93|
94|| Repo class | Path | Example |
95||:--|:--|:--|
96|| Multi-repo project (canon-extended, app, meta, …) | `{project}/worktrees/{repo}--{branch}/` | `hiresling.ai/worktrees/hiresling-app--feat-B90-01-L123-drafts/` |
97|| Single-repo / canon (e.g. `tortuga/`) | `{repo}/.worktrees/{branch}/` (gitignored) | `tortuga/.worktrees/chore/adhoc-L456-agent-system/` |
98|
99|The code blocks below show the multi-repo flow as default. For single-repo / canon, substitute `../worktrees/{repo}--{branch}` with `.worktrees/{branch}` and `cd {main-checkout}` with `cd {repo}` (the main checkout *is* the repo root). Parent dirs (`worktrees/` or `.worktrees/{nested}/`) must exist before `git worktree add`, `mkdir -p` first if needed.
100|
101|### Create (new branch)
102|
103|```
104|cd {main-checkout}
105|git worktree add ../worktrees/{repo}--{branch} -b {branch} origin/{integration-branch}
106|cd ../worktrees/{repo}--{branch}
107|```
108|
109|### Resume (existing branch with open PR)
110|
111|If the branch exists locally:
112|
113|```
114|cd {main-checkout}
115|git worktree add ../worktrees/{repo}--{branch} {branch}
116|cd ../worktrees/{repo}--{branch}
117|git pull --ff-only origin {branch}
118|```
119|
120|If the branch only exists on origin (no local ref yet):
121|
122|```
123|cd {main-checkout}
124|git worktree add ../worktrees/{repo}--{branch} -b {branch} origin/{branch}
125|cd ../worktrees/{repo}--{branch}
126|```
127|
128|### Work
129|
130|All reads, edits, commits, and pushes happen **inside the worktree**. Never in the main checkout.
131|
132|Commit at each task boundary, not at session end.
133|
134|```
135|git add {files}
136|git commit -m "{type}({scope}): {description}"   # Conventional Commits
137|```
138|
139|### Push
140|
141|First push:
142|
143|```
144|git fetch origin
145|git rebase origin/{integration-branch}
146|git push -u origin {branch}
147|```
148|
149|Re-push after rebase or amend:
150|
151|```
152|git fetch origin
153|git rebase origin/{integration-branch}
154|git push --force-with-lease origin {branch}
155|```
156|
157|Rebase conflict during push:
158|
159|```
160|# resolve conflict in file(s)
161|git add {resolved-files}
162|git rebase --continue
163|git push --force-with-lease origin {branch}
164|```
165|
166|### Monitor CI
167|
168|```
169|gh pr checks {PR-number} --watch
170|```
171|
172|Do not open a PR, request review, or proceed to the next task until all checks pass. If any check fails → fix, commit, push, rebase, repeat.
173|
174|### Open PR
175|
176|```
177|gh pr create --base {integration-branch} --title "{commit subject}" --body "Block: {block-id}"
178|```
179|
180|### Cleanup (after PR merges)
181|
182|Confirm the PR is merged before running:
183|
184|```
185|gh pr view {PR-number} --json state --jq '.state'   # must return MERGED
186|cd {main-checkout}
187|git fetch --prune origin
188|git worktree remove ../worktrees/{repo}--{branch}
189|git branch -D {branch}
190|git pull --ff-only origin {integration-branch}
191|```

194|
195|## Meta repos (`.repo-class=meta`)
196|
197|Meta repos (project knowledge bases, agent docs, logs, blocks) drop **only** the PR/staging ceremony, the worktree-mandatory rule still applies.
198|
199|Flow:
200|
201|```
202|cd {main-checkout}                                # meta repo root
203|git worktree add ../worktrees/{repo}--{branch} -b {branch} origin/main
204|cd ../worktrees/{repo}--{branch}

206|git fetch origin
207|git rebase origin/main

209|cd {main-checkout}
210|git worktree remove ../worktrees/{repo}--{branch}
211|git branch -D {branch}
212|git pull --ff-only origin main
213|```
214|
215|`.githooks/pre-push` template allows this when `.repo-class=meta`; for canon and app it enforces the PR flow.

{"content": "1|#!/usr/bin/env bash
2|# REPLICATOR: bring this machine to the agent environment declared in manifest.json.
3|# Idempotent. Safe to re-run. Reports what it would change with --dry-run.
4|# Needs: bash, git, python3, npm. Nothing else.
5|set -uo pipefail
6|
7|HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
8|MANIFEST="$HERE/manifest.json"
9|DRY=0
10|ONLY=""
11|SCAN=0
12|WRITE=""
13|ROLLBACK=0
14|RUN=""
15|APPLY=""
16|
17|for a in "$@"; do
18|  case "$a" in
19|    --dry-run) DRY=1 ;;
20|    --list) python3 "$HERE/lib.py" list "$MANIFEST"; exit 0 ;;
21|    --scan) SCAN=1 ;;
22|    --write) WRITE=--write ;;
23|    --only=*) ONLY="${a#--only=}" ;;
24|    --rollback) ROLLBACK=1 ;;
25|    --rollback=*) ROLLBACK=1; RUN="${a#--rollback=}" ;;
26|    --apply) APPLY=--apply ;;
27|    --help|-h) sed -n '2,8p' "$0"; echo; echo "  --dry-run   report, change nothing"; echo "  --list      print the manifest as a table"; echo "  --scan      report what this machine has that the manifest does not"; echo "  --scan --write  fold those findings into the manifest"; echo "  --only=X    run one section: harnesses npm repos files claude pi patches skills deltas host crew"; echo "  --rollback[=run] [--apply]  undo one skills run, skipping anything edited since"; exit 0 ;;
28|    *) echo "unknown flag: $a" >&2; exit 2 ;;
29|  esac
30|done
31|
32|CHANGED=0; SKIPPED=0; FAILED=0
33|step()  { printf '\n\033[1m== %s\033[0m\n' "$1"; }
34|ok()    { printf '  \033[32mok\033[0m      %s\n' "$1"; SKIPPED=$((SKIPPED+1)); }
35|did()   { printf '  \033[33mchanged\033[0m %s\n' "$1"; CHANGED=$((CHANGED+1)); }
36|warn()  { printf '  \033[33mmanual\033[0m  %s\n' "$1"; }
37|fail()  { printf '  \033[31mFAILED\033[0m  %s\n' "$1"; FAILED=$((FAILED+1)); }
38|# try <label> <cmd...>: run it, count it, and tell the truth about the result.
39|try()   {
40|  local label="$1"; shift
41|  if [ "$DRY" = 1 ]; then did "$label"; printf '          \033[36mwould\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; return 0; fi
42|  local out
43|  if out="$(eval "$@" 2>&1)"; then did "$label"; return 0; fi
44|  fail "$label"
45|  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -v '^$' | tail -2 | sed 's/^/            /'
46|  return 1
47|}
48|want()  { [ -z "$ONLY" ] || [ "$ONLY" = "$1" ]; }
49|
50|q() { python3 "$HERE/lib.py" "$@" "$MANIFEST"; }
51|
52|if [ "$SCAN" = 1 ]; then
53|  python3 "$HERE/lib.py" scan "$MANIFEST" $WRITE
54|  exit $?
55|fi
56|
57|if [ "$ROLLBACK" = 1 ]; then
58|  python3 "$HERE/lib.py" rollback "$MANIFEST" $RUN $APPLY
59|  exit $?
60|fi
61|
62|# Explicit crew rollout is isolated from package/config convergence and uses argv, not eval.
63|if [ "$ONLY" = crew ]; then
64|  if [ "$DRY" = 1 ]; then
65|    python3 "$HERE/crew_rollout.py"
66|  else
67|    python3 "$HERE/crew_rollout.py" --apply
68|  fi
69|  exit $?
70|fi
71|
72|for dep in git python3 npm; do
73|  command -v "$dep" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "missing required tool: $dep" >&2; exit 1; }
74|done
75|
76|# Check source consistency before the npm prefix setup or any other mutation.
77|if want skills; then
78|  python3 "$HERE/lib.py" farm-check "$MANIFEST" || exit 1
79|fi
80|
81|# npm's global prefix is often root-owned. Fall back to a user prefix so no step needs sudo.
82|if want harnesses || want npm; then
83|NPM_PREFIX="$(npm config get prefix 2>/dev/null)"
84|if [ ! -w "$NPM_PREFIX/lib/node_modules" ] || [ ! -w "$NPM_PREFIX/bin" ]; then
85|  export npm_config_prefix="$HOME/.npm-global"
86|  [ "$DRY" = 1 ] || mkdir -p "$npm_config_prefix/bin"
87|  export PATH="$npm_config_prefix/bin:$PATH"
88|  NPM_PREFIX_FALLBACK=1
89|  # Prepend it in the shell rc too, or a root-owned binary in /usr/local/bin keeps shadowing ours.
90|  for rc in "$HOME/.profile" "$HOME/.zshrc" "$HOME/.bashrc"; do
91|    [ "$DRY" = 1 ] && continue
92|    [ -f "$rc" ] || continue
93|    grep -q 'npm-global/bin' "$rc" || printf '\n# REPLICATOR: user npm prefix, must win over root-owned installs\nexport PATH="$HOME/.npm-global/bin:$PATH"\n' >> "$rc"
94|  done
95|fi
96|fi
97|
98|# ---------------------------------------------------------------- harnesses
99|if want harnesses; then
100|step "Harnesses"
101|[ -n "${NPM_PREFIX_FALLBACK:-}" ] && warn "npm prefix $NPM_PREFIX needs root, using \$HOME/.npm-global instead. Add \$HOME/.npm-global/bin to your PATH."
102|while IFS='|' read -r name version install manual; do
103|  [ -z "$name" ] && continue
104|  # An unpinned harness still has to install as something. "latest" is that something,
105|  # otherwise the command reads `pkg@unpinned` and npm 404s on a name it cannot parse.
106|  want_v="$version"; [ "$want_v" = "unpinned" ] && want_v=latest
107|  have="$(command -v "$name" 2>/dev/null || true)"
108|  if [ -n "$have" ]; then
109|    cur="$("$name" --version 2>/dev/null | head -1 | grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' | head -1)"
110|    if [ "$cur" = "$version" ] || [ "$version" = "unpinned" ]; then
111|      ok "$name ${cur:-present}"
112|    else
113|      if [ "$manual" = "1" ]; then
114|        warn "$name pinned to $version but installed by hand, upgrade it yourself"
115|      else
116|        try "$name $cur -> $version" "${install//\{version\}/$want_v}"
117|      fi
118|    fi
119|  elif [ "$manual" = "1" ]; then
120|    warn "$name absent. $install"
121|  else
122|    try "$name install $version" "${install//\{version\}/$want_v}"
123|  fi
124|done < <(q harnesses)
125|fi
126|
127|# -------------------------------------------------------------- npm globals
128|if want npm; then
129|step "Global npm packages"
130|installed="$(npm ls -g --depth=0 --parseable 2>/dev/null || true)"
131|while read -r spec; do
132|  [ -z "$spec" ] && continue
133|  pkg="${spec%@*}"; [ "${spec:0:1}" = "@" ] && pkg="@${spec:1}"; pkg="${pkg%@*}"
134|  if echo "$installed" | grep -q "/${pkg}\$"; then ok "$spec"; else try "$spec" "npm install -g '$spec'"; fi
135|done < <(q npm)
136|fi
137|
138|# -------------------------------------------------------------------- repos
139|if want repos; then
140|step "Tool repos"
141|BIN="$HOME/.local/bin"
142|[ "$DRY" = 1 ] || mkdir -p "$BIN"
143|case ":$PATH:" in *":$BIN:"*) ;; *) warn "$BIN is not on your PATH, these tools will not be callable" ;; esac
144|while IFS='|' read -r name url path bin; do
145|  [ -z "$name" ] && continue
146|  d="${path/#\~/$HOME}"
147|  if [ -d "$d/.git" ]; then
148|    ok "$name clone"
149|  elif [ -e "$d" ]; then
150|    warn "$d exists but is not a git clone, left alone"; continue
151|  else
152|    try "$name clone" "mkdir -p '$(dirname "$d")' && git clone -q '$url' '$d'" || continue
153|  fi
154|  for bin in ${bin//,/ }; do
155|  target="$d/$bin"
156|  if [ "$DRY" != 1 ] && [ ! -e "$target" ]; then warn "$name publishes no $bin at $target"; continue; fi
157|  if [ -e "$BIN/$bin" ] && [ ! -L "$BIN/$bin" ]; then
158|    warn "$BIN/$bin is a real file, not ours to replace"
159|  elif [ "$(readlink "$BIN/$bin" 2>/dev/null)" = "$target" ]; then
160|    ok "$bin -> $name"
161|  else
162|    # A symlink to the repo DIRECTORY instead of the binary looks fine to `ls` and fails on
163|    # every call. That exact break silently killed inbound hey beeps for a week.
164|    try "$bin -> $name" "ln -sfn '$target' '$BIN/$bin'"
165|  fi
166|  done
167|done < <(q repos)
168|while IFS='|' read -r name dest src; do
169|  [ -z "$name" ] && continue
170|  l="${dest/#\~/$HOME}"; target="${src/#\~/$HOME}"
171|  if [ "$(readlink "$l" 2>/dev/null)" = "$target" ]; then ok "$dest -> $name"
172|  elif [ -e "$l" ] && [ ! -L "$l" ]; then warn "$dest is a real file, not ours to replace"
173|  else try "$dest -> $name" "mkdir -p '$(dirname "$l")' && ln -sfn '$target' '$l'"; fi
174|done < <(q links)
175|fi
176|
177|# -------------------------------------------------------------- owned files
178|if want files; then
179|step "Owned files"
180|while IFS='|' read -r dest src; do
181|  [ -z "$dest" ] && continue
182|  d="${dest/#\~/$HOME}"
183|  s="$HERE/$src"
184|  if [ ! -f "$s" ]; then fail "$src is declared but missing from this repo"; continue; fi
185|  if cmp -s "$s" "$d"; then ok "$dest"; continue; fi
186|  if [ "$DRY" = 1 ]; then did "$dest"; printf '          \033[36mwould\033[0m copy %s\n' "$src"; continue; fi
187|  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$d")"
188|  # Back up whatever was there. We overwrite whole files here, unlike the deltas section.
189|  [ -f "$d" ] && cp "$d" "$d.replicator-bak"
190|  try "$dest" "cp '$s' '$d'"
191|done < <(q files)
192|fi

8|# Skill: Diagnose Root Cause
9|
10|Use this procedure when a bug is confirmed but the root cause is unclear, or when fixing the obvious symptom fails to solve the underlying defect. Do not guess; isolate the fault.
11|
12|## 1. Reproduce
13|
14|1. **Find the exact trigger.** Identify the smallest input, command, or state that reproduces the failure.
15|2. **Capture the failure.** Write a runnable check (a test, a script, or a single command) that currently fails and will turn green when the root cause is fixed.
16|3. **If you cannot reproduce it:** STOP. Search logs, traces, or session history for evidence. Do not attempt to fix a bug you cannot observe failing.
17|
18|## 2. Isolate
19|
20|1. **Halve the search space.** Use binary search (commenting out code, checking intermediate states) to isolate the subsystem or module where the failure originates.
21|2. **Find the boundary.** Identify exactly where the system transitions from expected state to corrupted state.
22|3. **Check the inputs.** Verify that the isolated subsystem is receiving the correct inputs. If the inputs are wrong, the root cause is upstream.
23|
24|## 3. Hypothesize
25|
26|1. **Formulate a hypothesis.** Based on the isolated boundary, state exactly *why* the failure occurs (e.g., "The cache key generator ignores the tenant ID, causing cross-tenant cache hits").
27|2. **Check the assumptions.** Verify the code against its documentation and its own tests. Are the tests wrong, or is the code violating the contract?
28|
29|## 4. Verify
30|
31|1. **Test the hypothesis.** Apply the minimal temporary change necessary to prove the hypothesis (e.g., hardcode the expected value). If the runnable check from Phase 1 stays red, the hypothesis is wrong; return to Phase 2.
32|2. **Implement the true fix.** Once the hypothesis is proven, remove the temporary change and implement the correct fix using `skill-amend-findings.md`.
33|3. **Prove the fix.** The runnable check from Phase 1 must now pass.
34|
35|## Failure handling
36|
37|- **The symptom moves:** If fixing the isolated bug reveals a new failure, the root cause was masked. Repeat the process on the new failure.
38|- **The system is untestable:** If you cannot write a runnable check, the system lacks observability. # GitHub Pull Request Workflow

Complete guide for managing the PR lifecycle. Each section shows the `gh` way first, then the `git` + `curl` fallback for machines without `gh`.

## Prerequisites

- Authenticated with GitHub (see `github-auth` skill)
- Inside a git repository with a GitHub remote

### Quick Auth Detection

```bash
# Determine which method to use throughout this workflow
if command -v gh &>/dev/null && gh auth status &>/dev/null; then
  AUTH="gh"
else
  AUTH="git"
  # Ensure we have a token for API calls
  if [ -z "$GITHUB_TOKEN" ]; then
    if _hermes_env="${HERMES_HOME:-$HOME/.hermes}/.env"; [ -f "$_hermes_env" ] && grep -q "^GITHUB_TOKEN=" "$_hermes_env"; then
      GITHUB_TOKEN=$(grep "^GITHUB_TOKEN=" "$_hermes_env" | head -1 | cut -d= -f2 | tr -d '\n\r')
    elif grep -q "github.com" ~/.git-credentials 2>/dev/null; then
      GITHUB_TOKEN=$(uv run python "${HERMES_HOME:-$HOME/.hermes}/skills/github/github-auth/scripts/git-credential-token.py")
    fi
  fi
fi
echo "Using: $AUTH"
```

### Extracting Owner/Repo from the Git Remote

Many `curl` commands need `owner/repo`. Extract it from the git remote:

```bash
# Works for both HTTPS and SSH remote URLs
REMOTE_URL=$(git remote get-url origin)
OWNER_REPO=$(echo "$REMOTE_URL" | sed -E 's|.*github\.com[:/]||; s|\.git$||')
OWNER=$(echo "$OWNER_REPO" | cut -d/ -f1)
REPO=$(echo "$OWNER_REPO" | cut -d/ -f2)
echo "Owner: $OWNER, Repo: $REPO"
```

---

## 1. Branch Creation

This part is pure `git` — identical either way:

```bash
# Make sure you're up to date
git fetch origin
git checkout main && git pull origin main

# Create and switch to a new branch
git checkout -b feat/add-user-authentication
```

Branch naming conventions:
- `feat/description` — new features
- `fix/description` — bug fixes
- `refactor/description` — code restructuring
- `docs/description` — documentation
- `ci/description` — CI/CD changes

## 2. Making Commits

Use the agent's file tools (`write_file`, `patch`) to make changes, then commit:

```bash
# Stage specific files
git add src/auth.py src/models/user.py tests/test_auth.py

# Commit with a conventional commit message
git commit -m "feat: add JWT-based user authentication

- Add login/register endpoints
- Add User model with password hashing
- Add auth middleware for protected routes
- Add unit tests for auth flow"
```

Commit message format (Conventional Commits):
```
type(scope): short description

Longer explanation if needed. Wrap at 72 characters.
```

Types: `feat`, `fix`, `refactor`, `docs`, `test`, `ci`, `chore`, `perf`

## 3. Pushing and Creating a PR

### Push the Branch (same either way)

```bash
git push -u origin HEAD
```

### Create the PR

**With gh:**

```bash
gh pr create \
  --title "feat: add JWT-based user authentication" \
  --body "## Summary
- Adds login and register API endpoints
- JWT token generation and validation

## Test Plan
- [ ] Unit tests pass

Closes #42"
```

Options: `--draft`, `--reviewer user1,user2`, `--label "enhancement"`, `--base develop`

**With git + curl:**

```bash
BRANCH=$(git branch --show-current)

curl -s -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: application/vnd.github.v3+json" \
  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/pulls \
  -d "{
    \"title\": \"feat: add JWT-based user authentication\",
    \"body\": \"## Summary\nAdds login and register API endpoints.\n\nCloses #42\",
    \"head\": \"$BRANCH\",
    \"base\": \"main\"
  }"
```

The response JSON includes the PR `number` — save it for later commands.

To create as a draft, add `"draft": true` to the JSON body.

## 4. Monitoring CI Status

### Check CI Status

**With gh:**

```bash
# One-shot check
gh pr checks

# Watch until all checks finish (polls every 10s)
gh pr checks --watch
```

**With git + curl:**

```bash
# Get the latest commit SHA on the current branch
SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD)

# Query the combined status
curl -s \
  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/commits/$SHA/status \
  | python -c "
import sys, json
data = json.load(sys.stdin)
print(f\"Overall: {data['state']}\")
for s in data.get('statuses', []):
    print(f\"  {s['context']}: {s['state']} - {s.get('description', '')}\")"

# Also check GitHub Actions check runs (separate endpoint)
curl -s \
  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/commits/$SHA/check-runs \
  | python -c "
import sys, json
data = json.load(sys.stdin)
for cr in data.get('check_runs', []):
    print(f\"  {cr['name']}: {cr['status']} / {cr['conclusion'] or 'pending'}\")"
```

### Poll Until Complete (git + curl)

```bash
# Simple polling loop — check every 30 seconds, up to 10 minutes
SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
for i in $(seq 1 20); do
  STATUS=$(curl -s \
    -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
    https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/commits/$SHA/status \
    | python -c "import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)['state'])")
  echo "Check $i: $STATUS"
  if [ "$STATUS" = "success" ] || [ "$STATUS" = "failure" ] || [ "$STATUS" = "error" ]; then
    break
  fi
  sleep 30
done
```

## 5. Auto-Fixing CI Failures

When CI fails, diagnose and fix. This loop works with either auth method.

### Step 1: Get Failure Details

**With gh:**

```bash
# List recent workflow runs on this branch
gh run list --branch $(git branch --show-current) --limit 5

# View failed logs
gh run view <RUN_ID> --log-failed
```

**With git + curl:**

```bash
BRANCH=$(git branch --show-current)

# List workflow runs on this branch
curl -s \
  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  "https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/actions/runs?branch=$BRANCH&per_page=5" \
  | python -c "
import sys, json
runs = json.load(sys.stdin)['workflow_runs']
for r in runs:
    print(f\"Run {r['id']}: {r['name']} - {r['conclusion'] or r['status']}\")"

# Get failed job logs (download as zip, extract, read)
RUN_ID=<run_id>
curl -s -L \
  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/logs \
  -o /tmp/ci-logs.zip
cd /tmp && unzip -o ci-logs.zip -d ci-logs && cat ci-logs/*.txt
```

### Step 2: Fix and Push

After identifying the issue, use file tools (`patch`, `write_file`) to fix it:

```bash
git add <fixed_files>
git commit -m "fix: resolve CI failure in <check_name>"
git push
```

### Step 3: Verify

Re-check CI status using the commands from Section 4 above.

### Auto-Fix Loop Pattern

When asked to auto-fix CI, follow this loop:

1. Check CI status → identify failures
2. Read failure logs → understand the error
3. Use `read_file` + `patch`/`write_file` → fix the code
4. `git add . && git commit -m "fix: ..." && git push`
5. Wait for CI → re-check status
6. Repeat if still failing (up to 3 attempts, then ask the user)

## 6. Merging

**With gh:**

```bash
# Squash merge + delete branch (cleanest for feature branches)
gh pr merge --squash --delete-branch

# Enable auto-merge (merges when all checks pass)
gh pr merge --auto --squash --delete-branch
```

**With git + curl:**

```bash
PR_NUMBER=<number>

# Merge the PR via API (squash)
curl -s -X PUT \
  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/pulls/$PR_NUMBER/merge \
  -d "{
    \"merge_method\": \"squash\",
    \"commit_title\": \"feat: add user authentication (#$PR_NUMBER)\"
  }"

# Delete the remote branch after merge
BRANCH=$(git branch --show-current)
git push origin --delete $BRANCH

# Switch back to main locally
git checkout main && git pull origin main
git branch -d $BRANCH
```

Merge methods: `"merge"` (merge commit), `"squash"`, `"rebase"`

### Enable Auto-Merge (curl)

```bash
# Auto-merge requires the repo to have it enabled in settings.
# This uses the GraphQL API since REST doesn't support auto-merge.
PR_NODE_ID=$(curl -s \
  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/pulls/$PR_NUMBER \
  | python -c "import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)['node_id'])")

curl -s -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  https://api.github.com/graphql \
  -d "{\"query\": \"mutation { enablePullRequestAutoMerge(input: {pullRequestId: \\\"$PR_NODE_ID\\\", mergeMethod: SQUASH}) { clientMutationId } }\"}"
```

## 7. Complete Workflow Example

```bash
# 1. Start from clean main
git checkout main && git pull origin main

# 2. Branch
git checkout -b fix/login-redirect-bug

# 3. (Agent makes code changes with file tools)

# 4. Commit
git add src/auth/login.py tests/test_login.py
git commit -m "fix: correct redirect URL after login

Preserves the ?next= parameter instead of always redirecting to /dashboard."

# 5. Push
git push -u origin HEAD

# 6. Create PR (picks gh or curl based on what's available)
# ... (see Section 3)

# 7. Monitor CI (see Section 4)

# 8. Merge when green (see Section 6)
```

## Useful PR Commands Reference

| Action | gh | git + curl |
|--------|-----|-----------|
| List my PRs | `gh pr list --author @me` | `curl -s -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" "https://api.github.com/repos/$OWNER/$REPO/pulls?state=open"` |
| View PR diff | `gh pr diff` | `git diff main...HEAD` (local) or `curl -H "Accept: application/vnd.github.diff" ...` |
| Add comment | `gh pr comment N --body "..."` | `curl -X POST .../issues/N/comments -d '{"body":"..."}'` |
| Request review | `gh pr edit N --add-reviewer user` | `curl -X POST .../pulls/N/requested_reviewers -d '{"reviewers":["user"]}'` |
| Close PR | `gh pr close N` | `curl -X PATCH .../pulls/N -d '{"state":"closed"}'` |
| Check out someone's PR | `gh pr checkout N` | `git fetch origin pull/N/head:pr-N && git checkout pr-N` |

# Hermes Agent

Hermes Agent is an open-source AI agent framework by Nous Research that runs in your terminal, a native desktop app, messaging platforms, and IDEs. It's in the same category as Claude Code (Anthropic), Codex (OpenAI), and OpenClaw — autonomous coding and task-execution agents that use tool calling to interact with your system. Hermes works with any LLM provider (OpenRouter, Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, DeepSeek, xAI, local models, and 20+ others) and runs on Linux, macOS, Windows, and WSL.

What makes Hermes different:

- **Self-improving through skills** — Hermes learns from experience by saving reusable procedures as skills that load into future sessions.
- **Persistent memory across sessions** — remembers who you are, your preferences, environment details, and lessons learned. Pluggable memory backends.
- **Multi-platform gateway** — the same agent runs on Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, iMessage, Signal, Matrix, Teams, Email, and a dozen more platforms with full tool access, not just chat.
- **Many surfaces** — the same agent core drives the CLI, the Ink TUI, a native Electron desktop app, a web dashboard, and an ACP server for IDEs (VS Code / Zed / JetBrains).
- **Provider-agnostic** — swap models and providers mid-workflow; credential pools rotate across multiple API keys automatically.
- **Profiles** — run multiple independent Hermes instances with isolated configs, sessions, skills, and memory.
- **Extensible & themeable** — plugins, MCP servers, custom tools, webhook triggers, cron scheduling, skins that theme every surface, desktop UI plugins, TUI widgets, and pet mascots.

**This skill is a hub.** The body covers identity, quick start, spawning/orchestration, and hard invariants. Everything else lives in reference files — **load the matching reference (below) before answering**; do not answer detail questions from the body alone.

**Docs:** https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/

## Scope & Verification

This skill is a concise operating guide, not the complete source of truth for every Hermes feature. If a Hermes feature, command, or setting is not mentioned here or in a reference, do not treat that absence as evidence that it does not exist. Check the live repository and official docs before giving a negative answer.

Good verification targets, cheapest first:

- **Every shipped feature, one line each: https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/llms.txt.** Start here for any "can Hermes do X?" or "how do I do X?" — it indexes the entire documentation set with a link to the page that answers. It is generated from the docs tree on every build, so it is never behind the product. Fetch it with `web_extract`, or `curl -s https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/llms.txt` when web tools are off. The whole documentation set in one file is at `/docs/llms-full.txt`.
- CLI commands: `hermes --help`, `hermes <command> --help`, and `hermes_cli/main.py`
- Source tree: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent

Never answer "Hermes can't do that" from memory. Hermes ships far more than this skill body describes, and the index exists so a negative answer is always checkable.

## Quick Start

```bash
# Install (shell installer — bootstraps PM, Python, dependencies, and the launcher)
curl -fsSL https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/install.sh | bash

# Interactive chat (default surface; set display.interface: tui to launch the Ink TUI instead)
hermes

# Single query
hermes chat -q "What is the capital of France?"

# Setup wizard  /  pick model+provider  /  health check
hermes setup
hermes model
hermes doctor

# Other surfaces
hermes desktop                 # launch the native desktop app (alias: hermes gui)
hermes dashboard               # web admin panel + embedded chat
hermes proxy                   # OpenAI-compatible local proxy backed by your OAuth provider
```

## Key Paths

```
~/.hermes/config.yaml       Main configuration (settings — never secrets)
~/.hermes/.env              API keys and secrets ONLY (under $HERMES_HOME if set)
$HERMES_HOME/skills/        Installed skills
~/.hermes/skins/            Custom themes (see references/themes.md)
~/.hermes/desktop-plugins/  Desktop app UI plugins (see references/desktop-plugins.md)
~/.hermes/tui-widgets/      TUI widget apps (see references/tui-widgets.md)
~/.hermes/pets/             Installed pet mascots (see references/petdex.md)
~/.hermes/state.db          Canonical session store (SQLite + FTS5)
~/.hermes/sessions/         Gateway routing index, request dumps, *.jsonl transcripts
~/.hermes/logs/             Gateway and error logs
~/.hermes/auth.json         OAuth tokens and credential pools
~/.hermes/hermes-agent/     Source code (if git-installed)
```

Profiles use `~/.hermes/profiles/<name>/` with the same layout. When a profile is active, resolve the real home from `$HERMES_HOME` — never hardcode `~/.hermes`.
